topic: Your car goes into the water: wait for it to fill, or open the window?
title: Your Car Is Sinking
idea: You have about a minute while the car floats, and waiting for it to fill is the mistake.
hook: Your car is sinking. Wait it out, or open the window?

beats.line: Wait means letting it fill, then pushing the door open.
beats.see: Card A WAIT highlighted; inside the car water rises from the floor while the driver sits with a hand on the door handle. Water starts on 'fill', hand pushes on 'door'.

beats.line: But water outside holds the door shut.
beats.see: Outside view: big blue arrows of water press flat against the door; it will not budge. Arrows slam on 'holds', door locks on 'shut'.

beats.line: By the time it fills, the car is deep and you have one breath.
beats.see: Car sinks down a depth ruler; inside, the air bubble shrinks to a single breath cloud at the roof. Depth on 'deep', bubble on 'one breath'. Card A gets a red X.

beats.line: About four hundred people die in sinking cars in North America each year.
beats.see: Map of North America fills with 400 small car icons, counter ticks to 400. Counter on 'four hundred'.

beats.line: It's the window. You get about a minute before water reaches it.
beats.see: Card B WINDOW gets a green check; a one minute timer starts while water climbs the outside of the side window toward its bottom edge. Check on 'window', timer on 'minute'.
Step card 1 SEATBELT; buckle clicks open and the belt snaps back. Click on 'off'.

beats.line: Two. Window down, while the power still works.
beats.see: Step card 2 WINDOW; finger hits the switch and the glass slides down, dashboard lights still on. Glass moves on 'down'.

beats.line: Three. Out through it, children first. Don't stop to call.
beats.see: Step card 3 OUT; a child climbs out the window first, then the driver; a phone on the seat gets crossed out. Child on 'children', X on 'call'.

end.line: If you picked wait, you just spent your minute.
end.see: Back to the two cards; the timer on card A runs out to zero and the car slips under. Timer zero on 'spent', loops into the hook shot of the sinking car.

description: Your car is sinking. Wait for it to fill or open the window? You only get about a minute.

facts.claim: Waiting for the cabin to fill so the pressure equalizes lowers your chance: by then the car is deep and you have one breath. Water outside holds the door shut.
facts.source: McDonald & Giesbrecht, Aviat Space Environ Med 2013;84:498-510

facts.claim: About 400 people die in submerged vehicles in North America each year.
facts.source: McDonald & Giesbrecht, Aviat Space Environ Med 2013;84:498-510 (OK-number)

facts.claim: A car floats only about 15 to 63 seconds before water reaches the bottom of the side windows (about a minute).
facts.source: IAED 'Get Out Fast' https://iaedjournal.org/get-out-fast ; McDonald & Giesbrecht 2013

facts.claim: Protocol: Seatbelts off, Windows open, Out, Children first. Do not phone first.
facts.source: Dr. Gordon Giesbrecht, University of Manitoba (as listed in FACTS-batch-035-046.md)

facts.claim: Electric windows should still work if used quickly.

notes: Correct card: B WINDOW. 'About a minute' is the file's own rounding of 15 to 63 seconds; that is the upper end, so the timer graphic should not count a precise sixty. Children first is folded into step three (the four-part protocol in three numbered steps). Left out breaking the side window and the laminated windshield caveat to stay in the word budget; consider it for a follow-up. Big number: about four hundred deaths a year.
